You are writing one concise English prompt for an LTX 2.3 image-to-video workflow.
You will receive three keyframes in order: first frame, middle frame, final frame.

Goal:
Describe a single continuous video that naturally evolves from the first image to the middle image and then to the final image.

Rules:
- Preserve subject identity, clothing, props, lighting, scene geography, and visual style across all keyframes.
- Describe only visible actions, camera movement, and environmental motion.
- Use chronological language: first, then, as, while, gradually, finally.
- Favor smooth physical transitions and small natural movements.
- Avoid hard cuts, scene jumps, morphing artifacts, text overlays, logos, subtitles, or sudden camera changes.
- The three images are soft guide references, not separate shots. Blend them through continuous motion and consistent camera flow.
- Never describe the result as three scenes, three shots, a montage, a slideshow, or a sequence of still images.
- Maintain subtle motion between and after guide frames: breathing, hair, fabric, background movement, parallax, and gentle camera drift.
- Preserve the exact subject identity, clothing, colors, object shapes, composition, and scene layout from the guide images.
- Prefer small physically plausible motion over large transformations that alter the source images.
- Include a restrained cinematic camera move only if it helps continuity.
- If the user's direction conflicts with the images, keep the images visually consistent and use the user's direction as motion guidance.
- Output a single paragraph only. No headings, no Markdown, no quotes around the prompt.

User direction:

Create a natural image-to-video transition across the three keyframes.
Keep subject identity, clothing, lighting, environment, and camera continuity stable.
Use gentle continuous motion, no hard cuts, no sudden scene jumps.
Make this feel like one continuous camera take, not a slideshow.
Do not freeze on any keyframe. Keep small natural motion after each keyframe, especially after the middle image.
Avoid visible crossfades, page-turn effects, hard image replacements, or abrupt pose swaps.
Avoid stop-and-go timing, held frames, pulsing motion, and sudden acceleration near the guide frames.
Carry the camera motion and subject motion smoothly through each guide frame instead of landing on it.
Prioritize visual fidelity to the input images: preserve face identity, body shape, clothing details, colors, scene layout, and object geometry.

Locked-off camera and fixed framing. A single full-body desktop mascot performs exactly one clear jumping cycle in place while preserving the exact identity, face, proportions, colors, costume, outline style, and flat chroma-key green background from all four guide placements. Maintain one fixed canvas and constant subject scale throughout. In every generated frame, the entire character must remain fully visible: both horn tips, all hair tips, both wings, both hands, the complete skirt, both legs, and both feet stay inside the canvas and never touch or cross any frame border. Preserve visible uninterrupted green-screen clearance around the complete silhouette at all times. Begin exactly in guide 1 as the neutral pose, compress into a readable crouch and push off. Guide 2 at frame 24 is the one and only spatial apex of the jump: approach guide 2 smoothly and monotonically from below, pass exactly through its airborne pose with both feet separated from the baseline, never place any body part higher than its guide-2 position before or after frame 24, and never overshoot upward. Then descend monotonically with natural gravity and pass exactly through guide 3 as the compressed landing pose at frame 40. Absorb the landing, rise, and pass exactly through guide 4 at frame 48 as the original neutral pose from guide 1, with identical character center, foot baseline, body scale, posture, and framing. During the remaining eight frames after guide 4, remain settled at that neutral position with only minimal natural breathing and no horizontal or vertical drift. Keep the character centered with no horizontal travel, zoom, camera movement, reframing, or scale change. The four guides are mandatory temporal anchors, not separate shots. Use smooth continuous motion, a crisp complete silhouette, clear anticipation, ascent, one apex, descent, landing, recovery, and exact loop closure; no morphing, crossfade, subtle bobbing, static interpolation before recovery, border contact, body-part cropping, or movement away from the recovered neutral position.
